headline: Stocks rose about 0.6% Friday to cap a record-setting week, while the 10-year ticked up 2bp to 5.24% and container rates slipped 2%.
dateline: Monday, October 12, 2026 · closes as of Fri Oct 9

tape.why: First gain since Tuesday's record high, closing out a record-setting week. Humana jumped 11.6% on Medicare Advantage ratings, and tower owners Crown Castle (+15.6%) and American Tower (+9.3%) rallied after SpaceX announced a spectrum purchase.
Best of the big three on broad gains, even as wireless carriers sank on the threat of a new SpaceX competitor (Verizon −8.7%, AT&T −9.8%, T-Mobile −13.3%).
Recovered part of Thursday's 1.25% chip-led drop, rising with the broader market; up 0.6% for the week.
Small caps gained on the day but still finished the week down 0.9%, lagging as long yields held near multidecade highs (AP).
Eased as stocks rose; the volatility gauge closed below 15 for the week's finish (Investing.com/YCharts close).

Treasury par yield, up 2bp after intraday swings; it recently touched its highest level since 2002. UMich one-year inflation expectations rose to 4.7%, and the 30-year mortgage rate is at its highest in nearly three years.
Week of Oct 5, released Oct 6. A second straight weekly drop, but still about two-thirds above a year ago; next print Oct 14.

rtab.grp: SOFR · dates Oct 8 '26 / Sep 8 '26 / Apr 8 '26 / Oct 8 '25

fhlb: FHLB Topeka advances: Awaiting first FHLB Topeka rate email. The mailbox could not be checked this run.

freight.why: Week of Oct 5, released Oct 6. Relief for carrier tenants, but fuel is still about $2.49/gal above last year; next print Oct 14.

Week 40, posted Oct 6 (the latest weekly report found). Flatbed, the construction and equipment segment, is the tightest board, with a load-to-truck ratio of 44.1 vs 30.0 a year ago; van linehaul rose 12¢ to $2.25.

September, released Oct 6, the second-highest reading in four years. Transportation prices hit 92.7 and warehousing capacity contracted to 39.3, so overflow trailers and equipment keep pushing toward outdoor yards.
Assessment of Oct 8. Shanghai–Los Angeles fell 3% to $7,624 and Shanghai–New York 2% to $10,220, a modest easing in import costs after Golden Week.

also: Baltic Dry 3,002 (−2.2%, Oct 6, lowest since late August) · Initial jobless claims 197,000 for the week ended Oct 3 · Tender rejections about 14% (NTG, Oct 7) · Freightos FBX, NRF Port Tracker, Cass, ATA tonnage: no new figures confirmed this run.

rows.u: Wells Fargo kept its Buy rating on Oct 9. Q2 EPS of $12.76 beat the $11.53 consensus on 11.8% revenue growth, and 2026 guidance was raised in August; Q3 results come Oct 21 with the call Oct 22.

Wells Fargo kept its Buy rating on Oct 9. Shares are down from $156 in late August despite a big Q2 beat (EPS $1.43 vs $0.76 expected, revenue +20%); the consensus target of about $178 sits ~44% above the price. Q3 results expected around Oct 27.

Oct 9 close not confirmed (last confirmed: $16.85 on Oct 8, MarketBeat), down from about $20 in early September. Q2 EPS of $0.28 beat by 3¢ on 3.9% revenue growth; consensus is Hold with a $27 target, and Q3 results are expected around Nov 5.

news.h: 10-year ends the week at 5.24%; mortgage rates highest in nearly three years
news.p: University of Michigan one-year inflation expectations rose to 4.7%. Sticky long yields keep IOS acquisition and refinance math tight heading into Wednesday's CPI.

news.h: Fed minutes: most officials see another hike by year-end
news.p: The September hike to 3.75–4.00% was unanimous; next meeting Oct 27–28. Higher-for-longer keeps pressure on IOS cap rates and refinancing math.

news.h: The Fed is hiking into a CRE maturity wall
news.p: About $875B of CRE debt matures this year, and owners refinancing 3–4% loans face much higher costs. Expect more forced sellers and wider spreads on levered IOS.

news.h: LMI jumps to 70.2 as transportation capacity contracts for a 10th month
news.p: Transportation prices at 92.7 and capacity at 34.4 mean a tight truck market, which supports demand for trailer, truck and container storage yards.

news.h: Drewry WCI falls 2% to $4,351; Shanghai–LA down 3% to $7,624
news.p: Transpacific rates are easing from highs but remain elevated, keeping chassis and container storage near ports in demand.

news.h: DAT: flatbed is the tightest board heading into October
news.p: Flatbed linehaul is up 28% y/y with a load-to-truck ratio of 44. Construction and industrial freight is what fills contractor and equipment yards.

news.h: Tender rejections near 14%; about 16 carriers in bankruptcy or restructuring
news.p: Capacity is leaving, which firms up rates but raises default risk among small-carrier tenants.

news.h: USTR opens the next stage of the USMCA review
news.p: Comments are due Jan 12, 2027, and the U.S.–Canada tariff dispute continues. Cross-border lanes (Laredo, Detroit, Buffalo) drive IOS demand along border corridors.

news.h: Wells Fargo reiterates Buy on United Rentals and Herc
news.p: The Street still sees upside after Herc's slide from $156 to $124; equipment-rental branches are core IOS tenants, so Q3 reports (URI Oct 21, HRI ~Oct 27) are the next demand read.

news.h: Martin Marietta at a new 52-week low; Citi trims target
news.p: Aggregates names keep falling with long rates despite solid pricing. Public infrastructure work still supports equipment and materials yards.
